content.title: About
content.content: Canned bluberries are ripe berries harvested at peak ripeness, cleaned and packed in glass or metal jars with a light syrup or their own juice. The berries retain their sweet‑tart flavor, bright color, and most of their nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bluberries are considered a “super‑fruit” because of their high antioxidant content, especially anthocyanins.
Canning allows the berries to be stored for up to a year without losing flavor or most vitamins.
In the United States canned bluberries are commonly used in pies, desserts, and sauces.
Bluberries grow in northern regions of North America, Europe and Asia.
The syrup used in cans usually contains a small amount of sugar, but sugar‑free versions are available.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins help protect cells from oxidative stress and support eye health.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Flavonoids improve circulation and may lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Vitamin C source
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Bluberries provide potassium, magnesium and iron, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The syrup can increase the product’s calorie count; choose a no‑added‑sugar version if you monitor blood sugar.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to bluberries.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some brands add preservatives; check the label if you are sensitive.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned bluberries can be eaten straight from the jar, added to yogurt, oatmeal, smoothies, baked goods, desserts, or used as a topping for pancakes and waffles. You may drain the syrup and rinse the berries if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if mold or off‑odors appear.
